For next reviewers:

1. This is the `squid.conf` I used:

```sh
acl localnet src 192.168.0.0/16         # RFC 1918 local private network (LAN)

acl SSL_ports port 443
acl Safe_ports port 80          # http
acl Safe_ports port 21          # ftp
acl Safe_ports port 443         # https
acl Safe_ports port 70          # gopher
acl Safe_ports port 210         # wais
acl Safe_ports port 1025-65535  # unregistered ports
acl Safe_ports port 280         # http-mgmt
acl Safe_ports port 488         # gss-http
acl Safe_ports port 591         # filemaker
acl Safe_ports port 777         # multiling http

# Deny CONNECT to other than secure SSL ports
http_access deny CONNECT !SSL_ports

# Only allow cachemgr access from localhost
http_access allow localhost manager
http_access deny manager

auth_param basic program /usr/libexec/basic_ncsa_auth /etc/squid/passwords
auth_param basic realm proxy
acl authenticated proxy_auth REQUIRED
http_access allow authenticated

http_access allow localnet
http_access allow localhost

http_access deny all

http_port 3128

cache_dir ufs /var/cache/squid 100 16 25
```

2. Before to start `squid` it is necessary to create cache directory:

```sh
# squid -z
```
No issues with normal (i.e. without proxy) connection, will try with proxy as well.

issue_context.title: [Feat]: Connecting to ACLK via http proxy with user/pass is not working properly.
issue_context.body:
### Bug description

I have a server in an environment which does not have direct access to the internet, and direct access is established via a http proxy to another server.

I've successfully claimed the node via `--claim-proxy` argument on the kickstart script, but since then the server is listed as UNREACHABLE in netdata cloud app.

The proxy is already been set in `netdata.conf`, in the `[cloud]` section, with this format:

        [cloud]
                proxy = http://myuser:mystrongpassword@192.168.40.20:3128

Looking for problems, I've tried to find errors in the netdata `error.log` searching for `aclk`, and I found this:

```
2022-04-08 07:31:48: netdata INFO  : ACLK_Main : Attempting connection now
2022-04-08 07:31:49: netdata ERROR : ACLK_Main : Cannot resolve host '@192.168.40.20', port '3128': Name does not resolve (errno 11, Resource temporarily unavailable)
2022-04-08 07:31:49: netdata ERROR : ACLK_Main : Error connecting TCP socket to "@192.168.40.20"
2022-04-08 07:31:49: netdata ERROR : ACLK_Main : Error trying to contact env endpoint (errno 22, Invalid argument)
2022-04-08 07:31:49: netdata ERROR : ACLK_Main : Failed to Get ACLK environment
```

The line *Cannot resolve host **'@192.168.40.20'**, port '3128': Name does not resolve* was interesting, maybe NetData is not parsing the proxy url properly, as it's including the `@` (separating user:pass from ip:port) into the proxy IP address itself?


### Expected behavior

Netdata should be able to connect to Netdata Cloud via an authenticated http proxy (as mentioned in the [docs](https://learn.netdata.cloud/docs/agent/claim#connect-through-a-proxy))

### Steps to reproduce

1. Try to connect Netdata to Cloud via an authenticated HTTP Proxy
2. See that the node remains UNREACHABLE in Netdata Cloud app.
3. See `error.log`.


### Installation method

kickstart.sh

### System info

